anchors.name: Antalya
anchors.dateGuard: Dündar captured Antalya before 1321; Yunus branch administered it; Mahmud was ruler immediately before Dündar's 1326 capture/death.

anchors.name: Korkuteli/Istanos
anchors.dateGuard: Yunus son Hızır had an early-14th-century madrasa inscription at Istanos (1319).

anchors.name: Alanya/Alaiye
anchors.control: Karamanid-linked Alaiye polity; Mamluk suzerainty/coinage evidence
anchors.dateGuard: TDV records Karamanid control and Yusuf Bey in 1333; independent study reports coins of 1321, 1326 and 1329 in name of Mamluk sultan al-Nasir Muhammad.

anchors.name: Manavgat
anchors.control: southern frontier / control requires date-specific reconciliation
anchors.dateGuard: Later sources associate Manavgat with Teke and Alaiye; do not back-project later 1361-66 events.

anchors.name: Anamur-Silifke corridor
anchors.dateGuard: Do not infer a continuous 1326 polygon from later Karamanid expansion; retain as corridor/frontier until more date-specific evidence.

keyFindings: Antalya and Alanya must not be merged into one polity polygon in 1326.
Antalya belongs to the Hamid/Teke branch context; Alanya is separately tied to the Karamanid-linked Alaiye polity.
Dündar Bey's death is dated 1326 in TDV, while some older references give 1324; scenario reconstruction should not silently collapse this disagreement.

Alanya has unusually strong date-specific evidence because 1326 coinage exists in the name of Mamluk Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad, while 1333 Ibn Battuta records Yusuf b. Karaman as ruler. This supports a Karamanid-linked polity with Mamluk suzerainty/legitimacy signals rather than direct Mamluk territorial administration.
The Antalya-Alanya coastal road and maritime network should be represented separately from political ownership.
Later Latin/Kypriot attacks and later Teke/Alaiye arrangements must not be back-projected into the 1326 political layer.
modelingRules: Separate politicalControl from settlement, port, route, and externalSuzerainty.
Represent uncertain Antalya-Alanya inland boundaries as frontier bands, not artificial precise lines.
Do not use modern Antalya, Alanya, Manavgat, or provincial boundaries as 1326 geometry.
Do not promote geometry until independent historical-geography evidence supplies defensible boundary reconstruction.
